372588.title: The Erdős–Rényi random graph maximum likelihood threshold conjecture
372588.statement: Let $G$ be a random graph generated according to the Erdős–Rényi model $G(n,c/n)$, where $c$ is a fixed positive real number, and let $d$ be the minimum integer such that $G$ is $d$-independent. **Maximum likelihood threshold conjecture.** The maximum likelihood threshold of $G$ is $d+1$ with high probability. This conjecture predicts that the upper bound for maximum likelihood thresholds is sharp for Erdős–Rényi random graphs; it is supported by computational experiments, but no resolution is given here.

372609.title: The out-degree-three expansion conjecture for quasi-kernels
372609.statement:
Let $D$ be a sourceless oriented graph, and write $N^+(v)$ for the out-neighborhood of a vertex $v$ and $S(v)$ for the set used in the paper's preceding theorem. Assume that $D$ has maximum out-degree at most $3$.

**Out-degree-three expansion conjecture.** There exists a vertex $v\in V(D)$ such that

$$
|N^+(v)\cup N^+(S(v))|\geq |S(v)|+1.
$$

The conjecture is proposed as a strengthening of the proof of the paper's out-degree-three theorem and would provide a local structural condition useful for constructing small quasi-kernels. The supplied text does not establish it or give evidence of resolution.

372683.title: Codenotti–Santos–Schymura conjecture on covering minima of weighted terminal simplices
372683.statement:
Let $\omega=(\omega_0,\dots,\omega_d)\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}_{>0}$ satisfy $\omega_0\leqslant\dots\leqslant\omega_d$, and define the weighted terminal simplex

$$
S(\omega):=\operatorname{conv}(-\omega_0\mathbb{1}_d,\omega_1e_1,\dots,\omega_de_d)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d.
$$

For $i\in[d]$, **Codenotti–Santos–Schymura conjecture.** The $i$-th covering minimum of $S(\omega)$ is attained by projection to the first $i$ coordinates, namely

$$
\mu_i(S(\omega))=\frac{\sum\limits_{0\leqslant j<k\leqslant i}\frac{1}{\omega_j\omega_k}}{\sum\limits_{j=0}^i\frac{1}{\omega_j}}.
$$

The source says that the covering radius of every weighted terminal simplex is known and that this conjecture gives the other covering minima, with the case $i=1$ proved; the remaining cases are open in the supplied text.
372683.review_depth: literal plus targeted primary statement/context; depth and gaps specified in note
372683.assessment: Conjecture 5.3, every dimension d and 1<=i<=d, positive sorted real weights; covering minimum is with respect to the integer lattice. Coordinate projection gives the easy direction; arbitrary rational subspaces give the missing opposite direction. i=1 and i=d are source results, not eligible parameter instances.

372711.title: Rich flows for 3-edge-connected graphs
372711.statement:
Let $G$ be a **$3$-edge-connected graph**, meaning that deleting fewer than three edges does not disconnect it, and let its maximum degree be $\Delta$. A rich $k$-flow is a nowhere-zero $k$-flow whose absolute values differ on every pair of adjacent edges.

**Rich-flow conjecture for 3-edge-connected graphs.** Every $3$-edge-connected graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ admits a rich $(\Delta+3)$-flow.

This conjecture would substantially improve the paper's general linear bound for the more highly connected case. The source presents it as a belief, and no resolution is given.

372712.title: Logarithmic bound for confluent-edge-free flows
372712.statement:
Let $G$ be a rich flow admissible graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. A pair of edges is **confluent** when the relevant flow values coincide in the sense used by the paper; a nowhere-zero $k$-flow is a $\mathbb{Z}$-flow with nonzero edge values of absolute value less than $k$.

**Confluent-edge-free flow conjecture.** Every rich flow admissible graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ has a nowhere-zero $O(\ln(\Delta))$-flow containing no pair of confluent edges.

The source contrasts this with the linear behavior obtained when both confluent and contrafluent pairs are forbidden. It gives no proof or resolution of the proposed logarithmic bound.

372769.title: The comparison conjecture for $A_\alpha$-eigenvalue bounds
372769.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, with maximum degree $\Delta$, minimum degree $\delta$, and let $\alpha\in[0,1]$. **Comparison conjecture.** One has

$$
\alpha(\Delta+\delta)+\sqrt{\alpha^2(\Delta-\delta)^2+4\Delta(1-\alpha)^2}
\geq\alpha(\Delta+1)+\sqrt{\alpha^2(\Delta+1)^2+4\Delta(1-2\alpha)}.
$$

The inequality asserts that the lower bound involving both the maximum and minimum degrees is at least the previously known bound involving only the maximum degree. It is proved for regular graphs and was observed computationally for non-regular graphs with minimum degree greater than one; the general claim remains open.

372792.title: The biquadratic SOS rank conjecture for 3 by 3 forms
372792.statement:
Let a **biquadratic form** be a homogeneous polynomial of degree two in each of two variable vectors, and let its SOS rank be the smallest number of squares of bilinear forms in a sum-of-squares representation. Let $\mathrm{BSR}(3,3)$ denote the maximum SOS rank among $3\times3$ biquadratic forms. **The biquadratic SOS rank conjecture.**
For $3\times3$ biquadratic forms,

$$
\mathrm{BSR}(3,3)=6.
$$

The known bounds are $6\le \mathrm{BSR}(3,3)\le 8$, while the value $6$ is attained by a $3\times3$ simple biquadratic form. Determining whether every $3\times3$ biquadratic form has SOS rank at most six remains open.

372797.title: Baranyai's partition characterisation of (3,6)-tight graphs
372797.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph with at least $4$ vertices. A graph is **$(3,6)$-tight** when $|E|=3|V|-6$ and every vertex subset $U$ with at least two vertices spans at most $3|U|-6$ edges. For an edge $e$, write $(V,S)/e$ for the graph obtained by contracting $e$. A graph $H$ is **$(2,3)$-tight** when $|E(H)|=2|V(H)|-3$ and every vertex subset $U$ with at least two vertices spans at most $2|U|-3$ edges.

**The partition characterisation conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $(3,6)$-tight if and only if, for every edge $e\in E$, there exists a partition $(S_1,S_2,S_3)$ of $E$ such that

$$
|S_i|=|V|-i\quad\text{for each }i\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

$e\in S_1$, and each of the graphs

$$
(V,S_1\cup S_2),\qquad (V,S_1\cup S_3)/e,\qquad (V,S_2\cup S_3\cup\{e\})/e
$$

is $(2,3)$-tight.

This conjecture is proposed as a correction to a claimed combinatorial characterisation of minimal $3$-rigidity. The paper presents a counterexample to the earlier characterisation and suggests that the stated partition condition may provide the appropriate characterisation; its resolution is not established here.
372797.review_depth: literal plus targeted primary statement/context; depth and gaps specified in note
372797.assessment: Source Conjecture 5.1 retains the partition question; source (3,6)-sparsity uses the appropriate small-subset convention, unlike raw two-vertex bound which would prohibit any edge. K4 against the raw definition is only a wording correction. No counterexample to intended partition characterization; contraction parallel-edge semantics and matroid union remain gaps.

372894.title: Han–Zhao's exact minimum co-degree conjecture for Hamilton ll-cycles
372894.statement:
Let $k$ and $k/2<\ell<k$ be integers such that $(k-\ell)\nmid k$, and let $n\in (k-\ell)\mathbb{N}$ be sufficiently large. Define

$$
s:=\left\lceil \frac{k}{k-\ell}\right\rceil.
$$

For an $n$-vertex $k$-graph ${\mathcal H}=(V,E)$, write $\delta_{k-1}({\mathcal H})$ for its minimum co-degree.

**Han–Zhao's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta_{k-1}({\mathcal H})\geq \frac{n}{s(k-\ell)},
$$

then ${\mathcal H}$ contains a Hamilton $\ell$-cycle.

This conjecture proposes the exact minimum co-degree threshold in the remaining range $k/2<\ell<k$ with $(k-\ell)\nmid k$, extending the cases already resolved for several parameter ranges. The divisibility condition on $n$ is necessary for a Hamilton $\ell$-cycle, and the conjectured threshold is expected to be sharp.

373026.title: Zero-free disk conjecture for matching moment generating functions
373026.statement:
Let $F_{k,m,n}(t)=\mathbb{E}(\exp(t\cdot C_{k,m,n}))$ be the moment generating function of the minimum cost $C_{k,m,n}$ of a $k$-matching in the random bipartite matching model. **Zero-free disk conjecture.** The moment generating function $F_{k,m,n}(t)$ has no complex zeros in the open disk of radius $mn/k$ centered at the origin.
The point $t=mn/k$ is the location of the first pole of $F_{k,m,n}(t)$, so the conjecture is equivalently that the Taylor series for $F_{k,m,n}(t)$ and $\log F_{k,m,n}(t)$ have the same radius of convergence. The source presents this as a conjecture supported by numerical computations; no proof or disproof is given.
373026.review_depth: literal plus targeted primary statement/context; depth and gaps specified in note

373130.title: The tree-width two running-time conjecture
373130.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let ${\mathrm{tw}}(H)$ denote its tree-width, and let $M_H(n)$ denote the maximum running time of the $H$-process. **Tree-width two conjecture.** Every graph $H$ with

$$
{\mathrm{tw}}(H)=2
$$

has

$$
M_H(n)=O(n).
$$

Graphs of tree-width one are trees and have constant maximum running time, while complete bipartite graphs $K_{2,s}$ show that tree-width two can already give linear running time. The conjecture asserts that linear growth is the largest possible for tree-width two.

373145.title: El-Zahar's cycle-cover conjecture
373145.statement:

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{r}n_i=n.

$$
\delta(G) \geq \sum_{i=1}^{r} \lceil n_i/2 \rceil,
$$

then $G$ contains $r$ vertex-disjoint cycles with lengths $n_1,\dots,n_r$. This is the classical graph analogue motivating the paper's results on cycle factors in digraphs; the conjecture provides a minimum-degree condition for covering a graph with prescribed vertex-disjoint cycle lengths.

373206.title: The inverse Littlewood conjecture for dissociated dimension
373206.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}$ be a finite set of size $N$, and define $\dim A$ to be the size of the largest dissociated subset of $A$. Let $K>0$. **The inverse Littlewood dimension conjecture.** If $N$ is sufficiently large depending only on $K$ and

$$
\\|\widehat{1_A}\\|_1\leqslant K\log N,
$$

then

$$
\dim A\ll_K(\log N)^2.
$$

Furthermore, $A$ contains a subset of size $\gg_KN$ and dimension $\ll_K\log N$. This would sharpen the known upper bound $\dim A\ll_K(\log N)^3$ and match, up to constants, examples formed from a large arithmetic progression together with a dissociated set of size about $(\log N)^2$.

373215.title: Conjecture on the smallest positive zero of the transformed polynomial \widetilde\Xi_n
373215.statement:
Let $(\Lambda_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the family of polynomials defined by the paper's explicit-polynomial construction, and set

$$
\widetilde\Xi_n(x):=\Xi_n(\sqrt{x}).
$$

For each $n$, let $0<\beta_n<1$ denote the smallest positive zero of $\widetilde\Xi_n$. **Smallest-zero conjecture.** One has

$$
\beta_n\longrightarrow 0\qquad(n\to\infty).
$$

This asserts that the smallest positive zero of the transformed polynomial approaches the origin as the index grows. The supplied context contains a proof of the stated limit, but does not identify an external resolution; the parser marks the status as unknown.

373596.title: Ryjáček et al.'s minimum-degree conjecture for forbidden-star graphs
373596.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. It is **Hamiltonian** if it contains a cycle through all its vertices. The graph $G$ is ${K_{1,4},K_{1,4}+e}$-free if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to either $K_{1,4}$ or the graph obtained from $K_{1,4}$ by adding an edge between two leaves; $delta(G)$ denotes its minimum degree.

**Ryjáček et al.'s conjecture.** Every $4$-connected ${K_{1,4},K_{1,4}+e}$-free graph with minimum degree at least $6$ is Hamiltonian.

The conjecture extends the known result for $5$-connected graphs, where the minimum-degree bound $6$ suffices. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

373597.title: Ryjáček et al.'s line-graph minimum-degree conjecture
373597.statement:
A **line graph** is a graph whose vertices represent the edges of another graph, with two vertices adjacent exactly when the corresponding edges share an endpoint. A graph is Hamiltonian if it contains a cycle through all its vertices, and $delta(G)$ denotes its minimum degree.

**Ryjáček et al.'s conjecture.** Every $4$-connected line graph with minimum degree at least $5$ is Hamiltonian.

The source states that this conjecture is weaker than Thomassen's conjecture, which omits the minimum-degree condition. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
